chunks: From him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from al-Halabi, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he said:

Regarding al-Qabalah (land reclamation/lease), it is that a man comes to barren land and takes possession of it from its owners for twenty years. If it is inhabited and has 'Uluw (landowners/possessors), it is not permissible for him to take possession of it unless he takes possession of its land and rents it from its owners, and he does not include the 'Uluw in anything of the Qabalah, for it is not permissible.

And regarding the man who comes to barren, dead land, extracts it, flows its rivers, builds it, and plants it, what is due upon it? He said: 'Al-Sadaqah (the land tax).' I said: 'If he knows its owner?' He said: 'Then let him return its right to him.'
And he said: 'There is no harm if a man takes possession of the land and its people from the Sultan (ruler/government).'

And regarding the leasing (Muzara'ah) of the people of al-Kharaj (land tax) by a quarter, a half, and a third, he said: 'Yes, there is no harm with it. The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) took possession of Khaybar; he gave it to the Jews when it was conquered for him, by al-Khabr, and al-Khabr is the half.'

key_terms.اَلصَّدَقَة: Al-Sadaqah: The land tax or charity tax levied on reclaimed land.
key_terms.اَلْأَرْضَ اَلْخَرِبَة: Al-Ard al-Kharibah: Barren or uncultivated land.
key_terms.اَلْعُلُوج: Al-'Uluw: Landowners or possessors of the land.
key_terms.اَلْقَبَالَة: Qabalah: Land reclamation or lease, a form of agricultural contract.
key_terms.اَلْمُزَارَعَة: Al-Muzara'ah: Agricultural partnership or leasing where crops are shared.
key_terms.خَيْبَر: Khaybar: A historical region known for its fertile land, referenced as a precedent for land leasing.

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for reclaiming and leasing barren land in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the fiqh of *Qabalah* (land reclamation), distinguishing between barren land where the reclamer pays *Sadaqah* (land tax) and inhabited land where existing owners' rights must be preserved. It validates sharecropping agreements (quarter, half, or third) by citing the Prophet’s grant of Khaybar to the Jews, a precedent widely accepted in Shia jurisprudence as evidence for flexible agricultural leasing contracts.
